title: IELTS Reading: Foundations
description: Short academic texts with the question types of the Reading test, from B1 towards B2. Written for Bo-ok.

units.title: Bees on the Rooftops
units.goal: True / False / Not Given: tell what the text says from what it does not say.

blocks.text: Before you read

items.example: Bees pollinate many of the crops we eat.
A single hive can hold tens of thousands of bees.
Urban gardens are becoming more common.
There has been a sharp decline in wild bee numbers.
New hives may compete with wild bees for food.
There is little evidence that the plan works.

blocks.text: Bees on the Rooftops

Over the past twenty years, beekeeping has moved from the countryside into the city. In many European capitals, hotels, offices and even museums now keep hives on their roofs. Supporters say that city bees help to pollinate parks and private gardens, and that the honey they produce is a pleasant reminder of nature in a crowded place.

The trend began partly as a response to reports that bee populations were in decline. Many people believed that keeping more hives would help to solve the problem. However, scientists point out that most of the bees kept on rooftops are honeybees, a species managed by humans, and that the bees in real danger are wild species, such as many kinds of solitary bees, which live alone rather than in hives.

Some researchers now warn that too many honeybee hives in one area may even harm wild bees, because both compete for the same flowers. A study in one large city found that the number of hives had risen much faster than the number of flowering plants. The researchers did not measure wild bee numbers directly, but they suggested that cities should plant more flowers before adding more hives.

City beekeepers often reply that their hives also teach people about nature. Several rooftop projects run free classes for schoolchildren, and many visitors say they had never seen a hive before. Whether this educational value outweighs the possible harm to wild bees is still being debated.
Questions 1–5: True, False or Not Given?
TRUE if the statement agrees with the text, FALSE if it contradicts the text, NOT GIVEN if the text does not say.

blocks.statement: Beekeeping in cities has become more common in the last two decades.

why.tr: Metin "Over the past twenty years, beekeeping has moved ... into the city" diyor: son yirmi yılda yaygınlaştığı açıkça yazılı.
why.ar: يقول النص إن تربية النحل انتقلت إلى المدن خلال العشرين سنة الماضية، أي أنها أصبحت أكثر انتشارًا.
why.en: The text says beekeeping "has moved ... into the city" over the past twenty years.

blocks.example: Over the last two decades, rooftop gardens have become far more common.

blocks.statement: Honey from city hives tastes better than honey from the countryside.

why.tr: Metin bal hakkında yalnızca "pleasant reminder of nature" diyor; tadını kırsaldaki balla karşılaştırmıyor. Karşılaştırma yoksa cevap NOT GIVEN.
why.ar: يذكر النص العسل فقط كتذكير لطيف بالطبيعة، ولا يقارن طعمه بعسل الريف، لذا الإجابة NOT GIVEN.
why.en: The text never compares the taste of city and country honey.

blocks.example: The article does not say whether city honey tastes better.

blocks.statement: The bees that are most at risk are the ones usually kept on rooftops.

why.tr: Metin tam tersini söylüyor: çatılarda çoğunlukla bal arıları tutuluyor, asıl tehlikede olanlar ise yabani türler. İfade metinle çeliştiği için FALSE.
why.ar: النص يقول العكس: على الأسطح يُربّى نحل العسل غالبًا، أما المهدّد فعلًا فهو الأنواع البرية. لذلك FALSE.
why.en: The text says rooftop bees are mostly honeybees, while the bees in danger are wild species.

blocks.example: Wild bees, not honeybees, are the ones in real danger.

blocks.statement: One study showed that the number of wild bees in a city had fallen.

why.tr: Dikkat: "The researchers did not measure wild bee numbers directly" — araştırmacılar yabani arı sayısını ölçmemiş. Ölçmedikleri bir düşüşü "gösterdi" demek metinle çelişiyor: FALSE. (Metin bir şeyin yapılmadığını açıkça söylüyorsa NOT GIVEN değil FALSE olur.)
why.ar: النص يقول صراحة إن الباحثين لم يقيسوا أعداد النحل البري، فلا يمكن أن تكون الدراسة أظهرت انخفاضها. لذلك FALSE وليس NOT GIVEN.
why.en: The text says the researchers "did not measure wild bee numbers directly", so the study cannot have shown a fall.

blocks.example: The study did not measure the bees directly, so it could not show a decline.

blocks.statement: Experts agree that the educational value of rooftop hives is greater than the harm they cause.

why.tr: Son cümle "is still being debated" diyor: uzlaşma yok. "Experts agree" bununla çelişir: FALSE.
why.ar: الجملة الأخيرة تقول إن الأمر "لا يزال محل نقاش"، أي لا يوجد اتفاق. لذلك FALSE.
why.en: The last sentence says the question "is still being debated", so experts do not agree.

blocks.example: Whether the benefits outweigh the costs is still being debated.

blocks.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Rooftop beekeeping is the best way to save bees.
Rooftop beekeeping is popular, but it may not help the bees that need help most.

why.tr: Metin önce çatı arıcılığının popülerleştiğini, sonra asıl tehlikedeki yabani arılara yardım etmeyebileceğini (hatta zarar verebileceğini) anlatıyor. A metnin tersini söylüyor, C ve D metinde yok.

units.title: Losing the Dark
units.goal: Matching headings: find the main idea of each paragraph, not a word that matches.

blocks.text: Before you read

items.example: Artificial light changes how animals behave at night.
Dust in the air scatters the light in all directions.
The observatory was built on a mountain, far from any town.
Many birds migrate south in the autumn.
Shift work can upset the body's daily rhythm.
The new lamps are shielded so that light only falls downwards.

blocks.text: Losing the Dark

A  For most of human history, a clear night sky was full of stars. Today, many people who live in cities can see only a handful of the brightest ones. The reason is artificial light: streetlights, advertising screens, car parks and buildings send light upwards and sideways, where it is scattered by dust and water in the air. The result is a dull orange or grey glow above towns, known as skyglow, which can be seen from many kilometres away.

B  Astronomers were among the first to complain. Observatories that were once built far from towns have found the night sky growing brighter as cities spread towards them. But the problem is not only a scientific one. Many people living in brightly lit areas have never seen the Milky Way with their own eyes, and some writers argue that this is a real cultural loss, since the stars have shaped stories, calendars and navigation for thousands of years.

C  Wildlife is affected too. Many animals use natural light to find their way or to know when to feed and rest. Newly hatched sea turtles, for example, normally move towards the brighter horizon over the sea; on beaches near bright hotels and roads, some crawl inland instead. Birds that migrate at night can be drawn towards lit buildings, and many insects circle streetlights until they are exhausted.

D  Light at night may also matter for human health. Our bodies follow a daily rhythm that is partly controlled by light and darkness, and bright light in the evening, especially light with a lot of blue in it, can delay the release of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep. Researchers are still studying how much outdoor lighting, rather than phones and indoor lamps, contributes to this.

E  Unlike many environmental problems, light pollution is relatively easy to reduce. Lights can be shielded so that they point downwards, dimmed or switched off late at night, and chosen in warmer colours, which scatter less in the air. Some towns and parks have been officially recognised as "dark sky places" after changing their lighting, and they now attract visitors who come simply to look up. The darkness, it turns out, can return as soon as the lights are changed.
Questions 1–5: Choose the correct heading

The passage has five paragraphs, A–E. Choose the best heading for each paragraph from the list. There are more headings than paragraphs. Read the whole paragraph: a heading sums up its main idea, not one detail.

blocks.prompt: Paragraph A
options: i. A problem with simple solutions
ii. Where the glow comes from
iii. A loss for science and culture
iv. Confusing signals for animals
v. A possible effect on sleep
vi. Why cities need more light
vii. The cost of new streetlights

why.tr: Paragraf A ışığın nereden geldiğini ve havada nasıl saçılıp şehirlerin üstünde bir parıltı (skyglow) oluşturduğunu anlatıyor. vi seçeneği tuzak: paragraf ışığın gerekli olduğunu söylemiyor.
why.ar: تشرح الفقرة A مصدر الضوء وكيف يتبعثر في الهواء فيصنع توهّجًا فوق المدن. العنوان vi فخّ، فالفقرة لا تقول إن المدن تحتاج إلى مزيد من الضوء.
why.en: Paragraph A explains what produces skyglow: light sent upwards and scattered by dust and water.

blocks.example: The paragraph explains where the noise in the building comes from.

blocks.prompt: Paragraph B
options: i. A problem with simple solutions
ii. Where the glow comes from
iii. A loss for science and culture
iv. Confusing signals for animals
v. A possible effect on sleep
vi. Why cities need more light
vii. The cost of new streetlights

why.tr: Paragraf B iki kaybı anlatıyor: gözlemevlerinin gökyüzü aydınlanıyor (bilim) ve insanlar Samanyolu'nu göremiyor (kültür). "But the problem is not only a scientific one" cümlesi bu ikisini bağlıyor.
why.ar: تتحدث الفقرة B عن خسارتين: المراصد تفقد ظلام السماء (العلم)، والناس لا يرون درب التبانة (الثقافة). الجملة "But the problem is not only a scientific one" تربط بينهما.
why.en: Paragraph B covers observatories (science) and the Milky Way, stories and calendars (culture).

blocks.example: The closure of the library was a loss for the whole town.

blocks.prompt: Paragraph C
options: i. A problem with simple solutions
ii. Where the glow comes from
iii. A loss for science and culture
iv. Confusing signals for animals
v. A possible effect on sleep
vi. Why cities need more light
vii. The cost of new streetlights

why.tr: Paragraf C kaplumbağaları, kuşları ve böcekleri örnek veriyor: hepsi yolunu ışıkla bulan hayvanlar ve yapay ışık onları yanıltıyor. Ana fikir: hayvanlar için yanıltıcı işaretler.
why.ar: تعطي الفقرة C أمثلة السلاحف والطيور والحشرات، وكلها تهتدي بالضوء فيضلّلها الضوء الاصطناعي. الفكرة الرئيسية: إشارات مضلِّلة للحيوانات.
why.en: Paragraph C gives turtles, birds and insects as animals misled by artificial light.

blocks.example: Bright screens can send confusing signals to the brain late at night.

blocks.prompt: Paragraph D
options: i. A problem with simple solutions
ii. Where the glow comes from
iii. A loss for science and culture
iv. Confusing signals for animals
v. A possible effect on sleep
vi. Why cities need more light
vii. The cost of new streetlights

why.tr: Paragraf D melatonin ve uyku hakkında. "may also matter" ve "still studying" ifadeleri etkinin kesin olmadığını gösteriyor; bu yüzden başlıkta "possible" kelimesi var.
why.ar: الفقرة D عن الميلاتونين والنوم. عبارتا "may also matter" و"still studying" تدلان على أن الأثر غير مؤكد، ولذلك في العنوان كلمة "possible".
why.en: Paragraph D is about melatonin and sleep, and says the effect "may" matter: a possible effect.

blocks.example: Drinking coffee late in the day may have an effect on sleep.

blocks.prompt: Paragraph E
options: i. A problem with simple solutions
ii. Where the glow comes from
iii. A loss for science and culture
iv. Confusing signals for animals
v. A possible effect on sleep
vi. Why cities need more light
vii. The cost of new streetlights

why.tr: Paragraf E "relatively easy to reduce" diyor ve basit çözümler sıralıyor: lambaları aşağı çevirmek, kısmak, sıcak renk seçmek. vii seçeneği tuzak: paragrafta maliyetten hiç söz edilmiyor.
why.ar: تقول الفقرة E إن المشكلة "سهلة الحل نسبيًا" وتعدّد حلولًا بسيطة: توجيه المصابيح إلى الأسفل وخفضها واختيار ألوان دافئة. العنوان vii فخّ، فالفقرة لا تذكر التكلفة.

blocks.example: Not every problem needs an expensive answer; some have simple solutions.

blocks.text: Questions 6–7: Choose the correct answer

blocks.prompt: According to paragraph B, why have some observatories been affected?
options: They were built in the wrong countries.
Towns have spread closer to them.
Their equipment is too old.
Astronomers have stopped using them.

why.tr: Metin: "the night sky growing brighter as cities spread towards them". "spread towards them" = onlara doğru yayılmak. Diğer seçenekler metinde yok.
why.ar: النص: "the night sky growing brighter as cities spread towards them"، أي أن المدن توسّعت نحوها. الخيارات الأخرى غير مذكورة.
why.en: The text: "the night sky growing brighter as cities spread towards them". The other options are not mentioned.

blocks.prompt: What does the writer say about outdoor light and sleep?
options: The link has been fully proven.
It only affects children.
It is still being researched.
It is less important than skyglow.

why.tr: Metin: "Researchers are still studying...". A tuzak: "may" kelimesi kesinlik olmadığını gösteriyor, yani "fully proven" yanlış.
why.ar: النص: "Researchers are still studying...". الخيار A فخّ، فكلمة "may" تدل على عدم اليقين، فلا يمكن أن يكون "مثبتًا تمامًا".
why.en: The text says "Researchers are still studying" this. "May" shows it is not fully proven.

blocks.example: The effects of the new drug are still being researched.

blocks.text: Questions 8–10: Complete the sentences
Use NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

blocks.prompt: The glow seen above towns at night is called ___.

why.tr: Paragraf A: "a dull orange or grey glow above towns, known as skyglow". "known as" bir şeyin adını verir.
why.ar: الفقرة A: "a dull orange or grey glow above towns, known as skyglow". عبارة "known as" تأتي قبل الاسم.
why.en: Paragraph A: "a dull orange or grey glow above towns, known as skyglow". "Known as" introduces a name.

blocks.example: The yellow haze over the city is known as smog.

blocks.prompt: On some beaches, young sea turtles crawl ___ instead of towards the sea.

why.tr: Paragraf C: "some crawl inland instead". "inland" = kıyıdan iç kısma doğru, yani denizin tersine.
why.ar: الفقرة C: "some crawl inland instead". كلمة inland تعني نحو اليابسة بعيدًا عن البحر.
why.en: Paragraph C: "some crawl inland instead". Inland means away from the coast.

blocks.example: The storm moved inland and reached the capital by night.

blocks.prompt: Lights in ___ colours scatter less in the air.

why.tr: Paragraf E: "chosen in warmer colours, which scatter less in the air". Mavi ağırlıklı soğuk ışık havada daha çok saçılır.
why.ar: الفقرة E: "chosen in warmer colours, which scatter less in the air". الضوء البارد الغني بالأزرق يتبعثر أكثر.
why.en: Paragraph E: "chosen in warmer colours, which scatter less in the air".

blocks.example: The café uses warmer lights in the evening to feel more relaxing.

units.title: When Every Town Had Its Own Time
units.goal: True / False / Not Given and summary completion: follow a history text from cause to result.

blocks.text: Before you read

items.example: Check the timetable before you go to the station.
The city has a large network of bus routes.
The company adopted a new system last year.
Delegates from forty countries attended the meeting.
Sailors once found it hard to measure longitude at sea.
Driving on the left is only a convention.

blocks.text: When Every Town Had Its Own Time

Until the nineteenth century, time was a local matter. Each town set its clocks by the sun, so that noon was the moment when the sun stood highest in the sky. Because the Earth turns from west to east, noon arrives a little later the further west you go. In Britain, this meant that Bristol was about ten minutes behind London, and towns further west were behind by even more. For people who rarely travelled far, the difference hardly mattered.

The railways changed this. A train leaving London at a fixed hour would arrive in towns that kept different times, and printed timetables became confusing for passengers and dangerous for railway staff, who needed to know exactly where each train was. In 1840 the Great Western Railway began using London time across its whole network, and over the following years most other British companies did the same. This "railway time" was based on Greenwich, the site of the Royal Observatory.

Not every town welcomed the change. Some people saw it as London telling the rest of the country what to do, and for a while many places used two times at once: local time for daily life and railway time for trains. The clock on the Corn Exchange in Bristol still has two minute hands, one showing London time and the other showing Bristol time. It was not until 1880 that Greenwich Mean Time became the legal time for the whole of Great Britain.

Other countries faced the same problem on a larger scale. In the United States, where railway companies had used dozens of different local times, the railways agreed in 1883 to divide the country into a small number of time zones. A year later, at an international conference in Washington, delegates chose the meridian passing through Greenwich as the starting line for measuring longitude, a decision that later shaped the world time zones used today.

The story is often told as one of progress, and in many ways it was. Yet it also shows that something as natural-seeming as the time of day is partly a human convention. Standard time made travel and trade easier, but it also meant that, for millions of people, the clock no longer matched the sun.
Questions 1–4: True, False or Not Given?
TRUE if the statement agrees with the text, FALSE if it contradicts the text, NOT GIVEN if the text does not say.

blocks.statement: Before the railways, noon in Bristol came later than noon in London.

why.tr: Metin Bristol'ün Londra'dan "about ten minutes behind" olduğunu söylüyor: güneş Bristol'de en yükseğe on dakika sonra çıkıyor, yani öğle orada daha geç geliyor. Kelimeler farklı ama anlam aynı: TRUE.
why.ar: يقول النص إن بريستول كانت متأخرة عن لندن بنحو عشر دقائق، أي أن الظهر يأتي فيها لاحقًا. الكلمات مختلفة والمعنى واحد: TRUE.
why.en: Bristol was "about ten minutes behind London", so noon came later there. Different words, same meaning.

blocks.example: Lisbon is an hour behind Madrid, so the working day starts later there.

blocks.statement: The Great Western Railway was the first railway company in the world to use a standard time.

why.tr: Metin GWR'nin 1840'ta Londra saatini kullanmaya başladığını söylüyor, ama dünyada ilk olup olmadığını söylemiyor. "first in the world" bilgisi metinde yok: NOT GIVEN.
why.ar: يقول النص إن الشركة بدأت استخدام توقيت لندن عام 1840، لكنه لا يقول إنها الأولى في العالم. هذه المعلومة غير موجودة: NOT GIVEN.
why.en: The text gives the date the GWR adopted London time but never says it was the first in the world.

blocks.example: The article says when the bridge opened, not whether it was the first of its kind.

blocks.statement: Everyone in Britain was happy to accept railway time.

why.tr: Metin "Not every town welcomed the change" diyor ve bazı insanların bunu Londra'nın dayatması olarak gördüğünü anlatıyor. "Everyone was happy" bununla çelişir: FALSE.
why.ar: يقول النص "Not every town welcomed the change"، وإن بعض الناس رأوه فرضًا من لندن. عبارة "الجميع كان سعيدًا" تناقض ذلك: FALSE.
why.en: "Not every town welcomed the change" contradicts "everyone was happy".

blocks.example: Not every student welcomed the new rules.

blocks.statement: The second minute hand was added to the Bristol clock in 1880.

why.tr: Metin saatte iki yelkovan olduğunu ve 1880'de GMT'nin yasal saat olduğunu söylüyor, ama yelkovanın ne zaman eklendiğini söylemiyor. İki bilgiyi birleştirip yeni bir bilgi uydurma: NOT GIVEN.
why.ar: يذكر النص العقربين، ويذكر عام 1880، لكنه لا يقول متى أُضيف العقرب الثاني. لا تجمع معلومتين لتصنع معلومة جديدة: NOT GIVEN.
why.en: The text mentions the two hands and the year 1880 separately; it never says when the hand was added.

blocks.example: The guide mentioned the tower and the fire, but not when the tower was rebuilt.

blocks.text: Questions 5–8: Complete the summary
Use ONE WORD from the passage for each answer.

blocks.prompt: Before the railways, each town set its clocks by the ___.

why.tr: Paragraf 1: "Each town set its clocks by the sun". "set a clock by something" = saati bir şeye göre ayarlamak.
why.ar: الفقرة الأولى: "Each town set its clocks by the sun"، أي ضبطت كل مدينة ساعاتها حسب الشمس.
why.en: Paragraph 1: "Each town set its clocks by the sun".

blocks.example: Sailors once found their way by the stars.

blocks.prompt: Different local times made printed timetables confusing for ___.

why.tr: Paragraf 2: "confusing for passengers and dangerous for railway staff". Özette "staff" ayrı sayıldığı için boşluk yolcular.
why.ar: الفقرة الثانية: "confusing for passengers and dangerous for railway staff". الكلمة المطلوبة: passengers.
why.en: Paragraph 2: "confusing for passengers and dangerous for railway staff".

blocks.example: The new signs are confusing for passengers who do not speak the language.

blocks.prompt: Railway time was based on ___, where the Royal Observatory stands.

why.tr: Paragraf 2: "based on Greenwich, the site of the Royal Observatory". "the site of" = bulunduğu yer.
why.ar: الفقرة الثانية: "based on Greenwich, the site of the Royal Observatory".
why.en: Paragraph 2: "based on Greenwich, the site of the Royal Observatory".

blocks.example: World time is still measured from Greenwich.

blocks.prompt: For a while, many places used ___ times at once.

why.tr: Paragraf 3: "many places used two times at once: local time ... and railway time".
why.ar: الفقرة الثالثة: "many places used two times at once": التوقيت المحلي وتوقيت السكك الحديدية.
why.en: Paragraph 3: "many places used two times at once".

blocks.example: The shop shows two prices at once: in euros and in pounds.

blocks.text: Questions 9–10: Choose the correct answer

blocks.prompt: Why did the American railways introduce time zones in 1883?
options: A conference in Washington told them to.
Companies had been using many different local times.
Britain asked them to follow Greenwich.
Passengers refused to travel by train.

why.tr: Metin: "where railway companies had used dozens of different local times, the railways agreed...". A tuzak: Washington konferansı bir yıl SONRA (1884) yapıldı, nedeni olamaz.
why.ar: النص: "where railway companies had used dozens of different local times". الخيار A فخّ، فمؤتمر واشنطن جاء بعد عام (1884)، فلا يمكن أن يكون السبب.
why.en: Dozens of local times caused the change. The Washington conference came a year later, so it cannot be the cause.

blocks.example: Because each office used a different system, the company agreed on one.

blocks.prompt: What is the writer's main point in the last paragraph?
options: Standard time was a mistake.
Standard time was useful, but the time of day is partly a human agreement.
Clocks should follow the sun again.
Trade was more difficult after standard time.

why.tr: Yazar hem faydayı ("made travel and trade easier") hem de saatin bir uzlaşma olduğunu ("partly a human convention") söylüyor. A ve C yazarın görüşü değil; D metnin tersi.
why.ar: يذكر الكاتب الفائدة ("made travel and trade easier") وأن الوقت "اتفاق بشري جزئيًا". A وC ليسا رأيه، وD عكس النص.
why.en: The writer accepts the benefits but notes the time is "partly a human convention". D contradicts the text.

blocks.example: The new rule was useful, but it was still only an agreement between people.

units.title: Why We Put Things Off
units.goal: Yes / No / Not Given: tell the writer's opinions from facts and from what is not said.

blocks.text: Before you read

items.tr: erteleme huyu göstermek, işi sürüncemede bırakmak
items.example: I always procrastinate when I have to write a report.
It was a relief to finish the exam.
The deadline for the essay is Friday.
Perfectionism can stop people from finishing their work.
A big task can feel threatening at first.
It is easy to make plans but hard to follow through.

blocks.text: Why We Put Things Off

Almost everyone puts things off from time to time: the report that is due on Friday, the phone call to the bank, the exercise plan that will start "next week". For a long time, procrastination was treated as a simple problem of laziness or poor time management. If people only planned their days better, the thinking went, they would get things done. In my view, this explanation misses something important.

Many psychologists now describe procrastination as a problem of managing feelings rather than time. When a task makes us feel anxious, bored or unsure of ourselves, avoiding it brings quick relief. We tidy the desk, check messages or watch one more video, and for a moment we feel better. The cost arrives later, when the deadline is closer and the task feels even heavier. In this way, putting things off can become a habit that rewards itself in the short term.

This view helps to explain why procrastinators are often not lazy at all. Some of them work very hard on everything except the one task they fear. Students who delay an essay may be the same students who care most about getting a high mark, because the essay has become a test of how clever they are. Perfectionism and procrastination, surprisingly, often go together.

If procrastination is about feelings, then the most useful strategies are those that make starting feel less threatening. One is to make the first step very small: not "write the essay" but "write three sentences about the question". Another is to decide in advance exactly when and where a task will be done, using an "if–then" plan such as "If it is nine o'clock on Tuesday, then I will open the document in the library." Research on plans of this kind suggests that they can make people more likely to follow through. A third is simply to be kinder to oneself after a delay: one study found that students who forgave themselves for putting off revision for one exam put it off less before the next.

None of these methods is magic, and I do not believe that procrastination can be "cured" for good. But understanding it as a way of escaping uncomfortable feelings is, I think, more helpful than calling people lazy. It replaces blame with a question that can actually be answered: what is it about this task that I am trying to avoid?
Questions 1–4: Yes, No or Not Given?

YES if the statement agrees with the writer's views, NO if it contradicts them, NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks. These questions are about opinions: look for "In my view", "I think", "I do not believe".

blocks.prompt: Procrastination is mainly the result of poor planning.
options: YES
NO
NOT GIVEN

why.tr: Yazar eski görüşü (kötü zaman yönetimi) anlatıp "In my view, this explanation misses something important" diyor. Yani bu görüşe katılmıyor: NO.
why.ar: يعرض الكاتب الرأي القديم (سوء إدارة الوقت) ثم يقول "In my view, this explanation misses something important"، أي أنه لا يوافق عليه: NO.
why.en: The writer presents this as the old view and says it "misses something important".

blocks.example: Some say the problem is money; in my view, that explanation misses something.

blocks.prompt: Avoiding a difficult task can make a person feel better for a short time.
options: YES
NO
NOT GIVEN

why.tr: Metin: "avoiding it brings quick relief ... for a moment we feel better". "quick relief" = kısa süreli rahatlama: YES.
why.ar: النص: "avoiding it brings quick relief ... for a moment we feel better"، أي ارتياح قصير: YES.
why.en: The text: "avoiding it brings quick relief ... for a moment we feel better".

blocks.example: Eating sweets brings quick relief, but it does not solve the problem.

blocks.prompt: Students procrastinate more than office workers.
options: YES
NO
NOT GIVEN

why.tr: Yazar öğrencilerden örnek veriyor ama onları başka bir grupla karşılaştırmıyor. Ofis çalışanlarından hiç söz edilmiyor: NOT GIVEN.
why.ar: يضرب الكاتب مثالًا بالطلاب لكنه لا يقارنهم بأي فئة أخرى، ولا يذكر موظفي المكاتب أصلًا: NOT GIVEN.
why.en: Students are an example, but the writer never compares them with office workers.

blocks.example: The report talks about teenagers but does not compare them with adults.

blocks.prompt: With the right method, procrastination can be stopped permanently.
options: YES
NO
NOT GIVEN

why.tr: Yazar: "I do not believe that procrastination can be 'cured' for good". "for good" = kalıcı olarak. İfade yazarın görüşüyle çelişiyor: NO.
why.ar: يقول الكاتب: "I do not believe that procrastination can be 'cured' for good"، وfor good تعني نهائيًا. العبارة تناقض رأيه: NO.
why.en: "I do not believe that procrastination can be 'cured' for good" — "for good" means permanently.

blocks.example: He left the country for good and never came back.

blocks.text: Questions 5–6: Choose the correct answer

blocks.prompt: Why does the writer mention students who care about high marks?
options: To show that procrastinators are usually lazy.
To show that people who care a lot can still delay a task.
To argue that essays are too difficult.
To compare students with their teachers.

why.tr: Paragraf 3'ün ilk cümlesi amacı söylüyor: "procrastinators are often not lazy at all". Örnek, çok önemseyenlerin de ertelediğini gösteriyor. A metnin tam tersi.
why.ar: الجملة الأولى في الفقرة الثالثة تبيّن الغرض: "procrastinators are often not lazy at all". المثال يوضح أن من يهتم كثيرًا قد يؤجّل أيضًا. A عكس النص.
why.en: The paragraph opens with "procrastinators are often not lazy at all"; the example supports this.

blocks.example: She mentions her own exams to show that even good students feel nervous.

blocks.prompt: According to the passage, an "if–then" plan says
options: why the task matters.
how long the task will take.
when and where the task will be done.
who will check the finished task.

why.tr: Metin: "decide in advance exactly when and where a task will be done". Örnekte de saat (nine o'clock on Tuesday) ve yer (the library) var.
why.ar: النص: "decide in advance exactly when and where a task will be done"، وفي المثال وقت (الثلاثاء الساعة التاسعة) ومكان (المكتبة).
why.en: The text: "decide in advance exactly when and where a task will be done".

blocks.example: We decided in advance exactly when and where we would meet.

blocks.text: Questions 7–10: Complete the sentences
Use NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

blocks.prompt: Many psychologists see procrastination as a problem of managing ___ rather than time.

why.tr: Paragraf 2: "a problem of managing feelings rather than time". "rather than" iki şeyi karşılaştırır: zaman değil, duygular.
why.ar: الفقرة الثانية: "a problem of managing feelings rather than time"، أي المشاعر لا الوقت.
why.en: Paragraph 2: "a problem of managing feelings rather than time".

blocks.example: The problem is one of trust rather than money.

blocks.prompt: Perfectionism and procrastination often ___.

why.tr: Paragraf 3: "Perfectionism and procrastination ... often go together". İki kelime: "go together" = birlikte görülmek.
why.ar: الفقرة الثالثة: "often go together"، أي يجتمعان عادةً. الإجابة كلمتان.
why.en: Paragraph 3: "often go together" — two words.

blocks.example: Stress and poor sleep often go together.

blocks.prompt: A useful first step is to write ___ about the question.

why.tr: Paragraf 4: "write three sentences about the question". Sayı rakamla da yazılabilir; iki kelime sınırını aşmaz.
why.ar: الفقرة الرابعة: "write three sentences about the question". يمكن كتابة الرقم أيضًا.
why.en: Paragraph 4: "write three sentences about the question". A number written as a figure is also accepted.

blocks.example: Start small: write three sentences, then take a break.

blocks.prompt: In one study, students who ___ for delaying revision put it off less the next time.

why.tr: Paragraf 4: "students who forgave themselves for putting off revision". "forgive oneself for something" = kendini bir şey için affetmek.
why.ar: الفقرة الرابعة: "students who forgave themselves for putting off revision"، أي سامحوا أنفسهم.
why.en: Paragraph 4: "students who forgave themselves for putting off revision".

blocks.example: She forgave herself for the mistake and tried again.

units.title: Rethinking the Street
units.goal: Matching information and summary completion: find which paragraph holds an idea, fast.

blocks.text: Before you read

items.example: This street is for pedestrians only.
Cars dominate the city centre.
Through traffic now uses the new ring road.
She lives in a quiet district near the river.
Dense neighbourhoods make public transport easier.
There has been a shift towards working from home.

blocks.text: Rethinking the Street

A  For much of the twentieth century, cities were redesigned around the private car. Wide roads, large car parks and motorways running through city centres were seen as signs of a modern, efficient place. Streets, which had once been spaces for markets, play and conversation, became first and foremost channels for traffic. Pedestrians were pushed to the edges, onto narrow pavements and into underpasses.

B  In recent decades, a growing number of planners have begun to question this model. They point out that space in a city is limited and valuable, and that a lane of parked cars takes up room that could be used for trees, benches, cycle paths or outdoor cafés. They also note that traffic adds to air pollution and noise, both of which are known to affect health, and that streets dominated by fast cars feel unsafe, particularly for children and older people.

C  One well-known experiment is Barcelona's "superblocks". Much of the city is laid out in a regular grid, and the idea is to group about nine blocks together, keeping through traffic on the roads around the edge while the streets inside are limited to residents, deliveries and emergency vehicles moving at very low speeds. The first superblock opened in the Poblenou district in 2016. At the start, some residents and shop owners complained loudly, worried about access and lost business; over time, many of the freed-up crossings were turned into small squares with seating, play areas and plants.

D  A related idea, often called the "15-minute city", has been promoted in Paris and elsewhere. It suggests that most daily needs — work, school, shops, health care and green space — should be reachable within a quarter of an hour on foot or by bicycle. Supporters argue that this would reduce the need for long journeys and make neighbourhoods livelier. Critics reply that it is easier to achieve in dense, wealthy centres than in spread-out suburbs, and some have claimed, without evidence, that it is a plan to limit where people are allowed to travel.

E  What these approaches share is a shift in the question planners ask. Instead of "How can we move more cars through this street?", they ask "What is this street for?" The answers vary from place to place, and change is rarely smooth. But the debate itself marks a significant change: the street is once again being seen as a public space, not just a route from one place to another.
Questions 1–5: Which paragraph contains the following information?
Choose A, B, C, D or E. The statements are not in the order of the text. In the test, a paragraph may be the answer more than once.

blocks.prompt: local opposition that later gave way to something more positive
options: A
B
C
D
E

why.tr: Paragraf C: önce "some residents and shop owners complained loudly", sonra "over time" kavşaklar küçük meydanlara dönüştü. "opposition" = şikâyet, "gave way to" = yerini bırakmak.
why.ar: الفقرة C: في البداية "some residents and shop owners complained loudly"، ثم "over time" تحوّلت التقاطعات إلى ساحات صغيرة. opposition = الاعتراض.
why.en: Paragraph C: residents "complained loudly" at first; "over time" the crossings became small squares.

blocks.example: At first the plan met strong opposition, but over time people came to like it.

blocks.prompt: a description of how streets lost their earlier social uses
options: A
B
C
D
E

why.tr: Paragraf A: sokaklar bir zamanlar "spaces for markets, play and conversation" idi, sonra "channels for traffic" oldu. Pazar, oyun, sohbet = sosyal kullanımlar.
why.ar: الفقرة A: كانت الشوارع "spaces for markets, play and conversation" ثم صارت "channels for traffic". الأسواق واللعب والحديث استخدامات اجتماعية.
why.en: Paragraph A: streets were once for "markets, play and conversation" and became "channels for traffic".

blocks.example: The old square, once a place for markets, became a car park.

blocks.prompt: a mention of a false claim about a planning idea
options: A
B
C
D
E

why.tr: Paragraf D: "some have claimed, without evidence, that it is a plan to limit where people are allowed to travel". "without evidence" = kanıtsız, yani asılsız iddia.
why.ar: الفقرة D: "some have claimed, without evidence...". عبارة without evidence تعني ادعاءً بلا دليل.
why.en: Paragraph D: "some have claimed, without evidence...".

blocks.example: Some have claimed, without evidence, that the vaccine is unsafe.

blocks.prompt: reasons why space for parked cars could be used differently
options: A
B
C
D
E

why.tr: Paragraf B: "a lane of parked cars takes up room that could be used for trees, benches, cycle paths or outdoor cafés".
why.ar: الفقرة B: "a lane of parked cars takes up room that could be used for trees, benches...".
why.en: Paragraph B: parked cars take up "room that could be used for trees, benches, cycle paths or outdoor cafés".

blocks.example: The empty car park could be used for a weekly market.

blocks.prompt: a change in the basic question that planners ask
options: A
B
C
D
E

why.tr: Paragraf E: "a shift in the question planners ask" — "How can we move more cars...?" yerine "What is this street for?".
why.ar: الفقرة E: "a shift in the question planners ask"، فبدلًا من سؤال حركة السيارات صار السؤال: ما الغرض من هذا الشارع؟
why.en: Paragraph E: "a shift in the question planners ask".

blocks.example: The new manager changed the question from "How fast?" to "How well?".

blocks.text: Questions 6–8: Complete the summary
Use ONE WORD OR A NUMBER from the passage for each answer.

blocks.prompt: In a Barcelona superblock, about ___ blocks are grouped together.

why.tr: Paragraf C: "group about nine blocks together". Sayı rakamla da yazılabilir.
why.ar: الفقرة C: "group about nine blocks together". يمكن كتابة الرقم 9 أيضًا.
why.en: Paragraph C: "group about nine blocks together".

blocks.example: The school groups about thirty pupils in each class.

blocks.prompt: Through traffic stays on the roads around the ___.

why.tr: Paragraf C: "keeping through traffic on the roads around the edge". "edge" = kenar, çevre.
why.ar: الفقرة C: "keeping through traffic on the roads around the edge"، أي على الطرق المحيطة.
why.en: Paragraph C: "on the roads around the edge".

blocks.example: Lorries must use the road around the edge of the town.

blocks.prompt: Many of the freed-up crossings were turned into small ___.

why.tr: Paragraf C: "turned into small squares with seating, play areas and plants". "square" burada meydan demek; çoğul olmalı.
why.ar: الفقرة C: "turned into small squares". square هنا تعني ساحة، والكلمة بصيغة الجمع.
why.en: Paragraph C: "turned into small squares". Keep the plural.

blocks.example: The old crossroads was turned into a small square with trees.

blocks.text: Questions 9–11

blocks.prompt: What do critics of the 15-minute city say?
options: It is too expensive for wealthy city centres.
It works better in dense centres than in spread-out suburbs.
Cycling is too dangerous for most people.
It would make journeys longer.

why.tr: Paragraf D: "easier to achieve in dense, wealthy centres than in spread-out suburbs". A tuzak: "wealthy" kelimesi geçiyor ama anlam ters.
why.ar: الفقرة D: "easier to achieve in dense, wealthy centres than in spread-out suburbs". الخيار A فخّ: كلمة wealthy موجودة لكن المعنى معكوس.
why.en: Paragraph D: "easier to achieve in dense, wealthy centres than in spread-out suburbs". A reuses "wealthy" with the wrong meaning.

blocks.example: The plan is easier to achieve in small towns than in big cities.

blocks.statement: All residents supported the first superblock from the start.

why.tr: Paragraf C: "At the start, some residents and shop owners complained loudly". Bazıları baştan şikâyet ettiyse "all supported" yanlıştır: FALSE.
why.ar: الفقرة C: "At the start, some residents and shop owners complained loudly". إذا اشتكى بعضهم فلا يمكن أن يكون الجميع مؤيدين: FALSE.
why.en: "At the start, some residents ... complained loudly" contradicts "all residents supported".

blocks.example: Not everyone supported the idea at the start.

blocks.prompt: Which statement best sums up the writer's view?
options: Cars should be banned from cities.
Changing streets is simple when planners agree.
Rethinking what streets are for is an important change, even though it is not easy.
Every city should copy Barcelona's model exactly.

why.tr: Paragraf E: "change is rarely smooth" ama "the debate itself marks a significant change". Yazar arabaları yasaklamayı (A) ya da Barcelona'yı aynen kopyalamayı (D) önermiyor; "answers vary from place to place".
why.ar: الفقرة E: "change is rarely smooth" لكن "the debate itself marks a significant change". الكاتب لا يدعو إلى منع السيارات (A) ولا إلى نسخ برشلونة (D)، فهو يقول إن الإجابات تختلف من مكان لآخر.
why.en: Paragraph E: change "is rarely smooth" but the debate "marks a significant change"; answers "vary from place to place".

blocks.example: The reform is important, even though it will not be easy.
